subject: Phantom queue stall — FinnoHealth production impact
messages:
From: Tom Redd <tom.redd@finnohealth.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: sre@finnohealth.com, anna.carter@finnohealth.com
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 18:42:00 -0700
Subject: Phantom queue stalls — API returning 502s and timeouts

Hi Olga,

We're seeing intermittent large tail latencies against the Redwood endpoint (model: rwdbert-v2) over the last 3 deploy windows. Symptoms:
- Spikes in 95/99 latency to 10–45s for some user requests; other requests finish sub-second.
- A rise in 502/timeout errors in our frontend (~3.2% over a 30m window).
- Throughput appears to drop during each spike even though incoming request rate holds steady.

I attached two short traces and a sample of our proxy logs. This began around 18:30 PDT during our peak batch and recurred several times. We believe requests are piling up in some internal queue and then a subset exhausts a cap/timeout, leading to cascading failures.

We need an urgent triage and either a mitigation (increase concurrency cap / fallback routing) or a rollback. Our SLA is impacted. Can we get someone on a call?

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Redd
Head of Platform, FinnoHealth

Attachments: finno-prod-error-sample-logs.txt, trace-20280618-18-38.json

Tom —

Thanks for the quick heads-up and for the traces. I'm looping in David (runtime) and Marissa (CS) to triage. Quick read: I see repeated request IDs that hang in the "inflight" queue for 20–40s and then either timeout or get dropped. We'll validate whether this is a root-cause on our KV cache eviction, a concurrency cap we recently tightened, or a routing fallback path that misbehaves under load.

Immediate asks from our side:
- David: can you check kernel-level backlog and per-instance concurrency caps for the customer's dedicated pool?
- Marissa: please confirm whether Finno is on Dedicated or Hosted routing today and if they have any pinned variants.
- Tom: if you can share the HubSpot ID/route and the typical qps distribution that helps.

I'll set up a short call in 10m to gather live traces. If we identify a quick mitigation, we'll push a config change and monitor.

— Olga

Redwood Inference

From: david.kim@redwood.ai <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 19:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Phantom queue stalls — API returning 502s and timeouts

Quick notes from initial triage (runtime captures attached):

Observations:
- Several GPU workers in Finno's dedicated pool show an elevated backlog counter and a sustained increase in KV-cache misses at the onset of each spike.
- We recently lowered soft concurrency caps on the pool to enforce fair-share during high demand (rolled 2028-06-17 03:20UTC). That change correlates with the timeline.
- When the cap is reached, requests are queued at per-worker dispatch queues. We have a bug where a non-idempotent pre-filter can block dequeue under certain partial-failure paths -> leading to a "phantom" stall where the queue head cannot progress.

Immediate mitigations I can apply:
1) Temporarily raise the soft concurrency cap to previous value for Finno's pool.
2) Enable fallback to the warm standby variant in another region (adds latency but prevents 502s).
3) Hotfix the pre-filter guard (needs 2–3 hours QA).

I recommend (1) + (2) as an emergency posture and then schedule the fix.

Attachments: runtime-kernel-backlog-olga-trace-1806.txt

— David
David Kim
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: olga.petrov@redwood.ai <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: executive-team@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 20 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Phantom queue stall — FinnoHealth (exec brief)

Executive summary for visibility:

What happened:
- Customer FinnoHealth saw intermittent long-tail latencies leading to ~3% 502/timeout errors during peak on 2028-06-18 evening PDT. Root cause is a previously unknown interaction between a recent soft-concurrency cap change and a request pre-filter that can block dequeues in rare partial-failure paths. This produced a "phantom" head-of-queue stall on some workers.

Impact:
- Customer-facing errors and degraded throughput for FinnoHealth customers; estimated revenue impact is low but SLA credit conversation likely.
- Affected a single dedicated pool (no cross-customer blast radius).

Immediate remediation taken:
- Soft concurrency cap reverted to previous levels for Finno's pool (rolled 2028-06-18 19:26 PDT).
- Cross-region fallback enabled for the impacted route while monitoring.
- Customer notified and provided traces; CS coordinated mitigations.

Next steps / owner:
- Runtime team (David Kim) to ship pre-filter robustness fix and test (ETA 2–3 business hours for hotfix test, full rollout 48 hours).
- Product & Ops (Olga) to run a short retrospective and propose guardrails to catch queueing regressions in deploy gates.
- CS (Marissa) to coordinate SLA conversation with FinnoHealth and record credits if required.

Attachments and links: runtime-kernel-backlog-olga-trace-1806.txt; JIRA-RI-1249; https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1Finno-Incident

I recommend we treat this as a P1 for the runtime fix given the potential for similar regressions when making cap-related changes.

— Olga
Olga Petrov
Senior Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
